title: A Dioscorides entry branches one root into preparations, effects, and an overdose result
summary: Dioscorides' Meum entry explicitly gives boiled or pounded roots, honey syrup, hip bath, plaster, and an excessive-decoction adverse effect. The content distinction is branch structure, not repeated plant-name equality.

design.mechanism: One source item is carried through alternative preparation operators; each branch has a distinct application/result, and an excess condition reverses the ordinary benefit with a named harm.
design.source_example: Dioscorides, De materia medica I.3 (UPenn/Gunther edition, printed p. 5): Meum roots are boiled or pounded and drunk; pounded with honey as syrup; boiled for a hip bath; plastered on children; too much decoction causes headache.
design.target_endpoint: Already admitted Herbal complete-paragraph cache; no target text, labels, or new selectors were opened.

two_readings.name: branching preparation record
consequences: A repeated material core may feed different operation/application slots, with downstream result type changing by branch.
An explicit excess/exception branch must produce an adverse result rather than the ordinary treatment outcome.

two_readings.name: static item and procedure list
consequences: The same material can recur beside unrelated procedures without a shared branch source.
The adverse statement is an independent warning and need not be tied to the preceding preparation or result.

design.smallest_distinguishing_observation: A complete target record would need one reused material component linked to at least two distinct preparation/application roles and a separately marked conditional reversal; exact whole-word identity is unnecessary, but the branch and result positions must be fixed before reading.
design.nearest_rival: A plant/material catalogue with neighboring preparation notes, where shared material forms reflect editorial reuse rather than one item branching through state and outcome.
assumption_costs: The target contains complete Herbal records with independently recognizable branch and result positions.
A first-century Greek pharmacological entry is a relevant content analogue for the manuscript.
The 1933 English translation is treated as a guide to relations, not a target lexicon or modern plant identification.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The target has no independently bound adverse-result or preparation branch marker; any apparent repeated core could be ordinary component reuse and the source cannot select among content genres.
design.falsifier: A source-frozen target model repeatedly links the same material component to only one role or treats an independently marked excess branch as the same result without an explicit exception operator.

primary_sources.locator: Dioscorides, De materia medica I.3 Meum, printed p. 5
primary_sources.source_limit: English translation/edition based on John Goodyer's 1655 translation and Gunther's 1933 edition; exact Greek wording and plant identity remain outside this card.
